The Surrogate Mother

Freida McFadden

3.88
457,121 ratings30,508 reviews
Rate this book
From the #1 Sunday Times bestselling author of The Housemaid, The Boyfriend, and The Tenant comes a story of monstrous motherhood. She gave you a life. Now she wants yours.

She was promised a miracle. She got more than she bargained for.

Abby wants a baby more than anything.

But after years of failed infertility treatments and adoptions that have fallen through, it seems like motherhood is not in her future.

That is, until her personal assistant Monica makes a generous offer to serve as a surrogate. It’s an offer that will make all of Abby's dreams come true.

But soon, strange things start happening. And it turns out Monica isn't who she says she is. The woman now carrying Abby's child has an unspeakable secret.

And she will stop at nothing to get what she wants.

Freida McFadden delivers a page-turner that redefines what it means to be in the family way, with gut-wrenching twists and pulse-pounding thrills that will keep you hooked until the suspenseful conclusion.

About the author

Freida McFadden

108 books309k followers
#1 New York Times, USA Today, Wall Street Journal, Publisher's Weekly, and Amazon Charts bestselling author Freida McFadden is a practicing physician specializing in brain injury who has penned multiple Kindle bestselling psychological thrillers and medical humor novels. She lives with her family and possessed cat in a centuries-old three-story home overlooking the ocean, with staircases that creak and moan with each step, and nobody could hear you if you scream. Unless you scream really loudly, maybe.

March 4, 2022
I almost want to write an unwarned spoiler here just to save someone the time…. But I won’t… What I WILL say is this: I’ve read at least 5 books by Frieda and I think at this point I can confidently say… this will probably be my last. The plots of her books are always what draw me in… that coupled with what always guarantees to be a fast paced, page turner — I always truly, truly, WANT to enjoy her books but alas… the way she writes her characters, particularly the women is always just so… mind-numbingly… STUPID. Like unbelievably so. The point of a psychological thriller is of course meant to have you questioning everyone, even your own instincts but the way she writes it is never realistic. She makes her characters ENTIRELY too naive every time just for the sake of frustrating the reader. I get it, books are supposed to evoke emotion but after reading multiples and getting a feel for her writing style… the bread and butter of the “psychological” part is simply making the scenarios so left field that you end up wanting to scream. The only reason I finished this book was to see how it ended. We got a nice little plot twist in the end but it still was so far fetched I rolled my eyes… and this coming from someone who enjoys reading sci-fi and fantasy as well. The only “thriller” part of this book was being done.

And Yikes… I know this is harsh but… I’m so irritated with this book. I would only recommend her books to those who are not avid readers of the genre… its faced paced and crazy enough to keep the occasional reader’s attention… but if you are a hard core psy-thriller reader, save your nerves.

I’ll admit it—I’m a full-blown Freida McFadden addict. I devour her fast-paced thrillers like they’re slices of Basque burnt cheesecake: indulgent, intense, and totally addictive. Her books are my ultimate guilty pleasure, especially when they come with those signature sucker-punch twists that leave you wide-eyed and whispering, “Wait—what?!”

This one, originally published in 2018, is one of her earlier works, and when I saw it pop up on NetGalley, I didn’t hesitate. I clicked request faster than you can say “domestic thriller.” Now, is it as mind-bending as her more recent releases? Not quite. You can see some of the turns coming, and the twist doesn’t knock you flat like her latest jaw-droppers—but that’s okay. You can already sense the McFadden magic brewing here, and it’s wildly entertaining from start to finish.

Our main character Abby has all the hallmark traits of a McFadden heroine: a little too trusting, a little too naïve, kind of like a Disney princess crossed with a toothpaste commercial—smiling brightly while chaos brews behind her. And then there’s her husband Sam. Oh, Sam. He commits the cardinal sin of marriage: believing a stranger over his own wife. Boo, Sam. Instant deduction of husband points. You broke the sacred rule: the wife is always right!

The plot? Deliciously chaotic. Abby has the perfect life on paper: a successful career, a charming professor husband, and a dream of starting a family. After fertility struggles and a failed adoption, hope seems lost—until her sweet, seemingly selfless assistant Monica offers to be their surrogate in exchange for help pursuing her dreams in graphic design school. Sounds like a dream, right? Well… no surprise here—things spiral quickly. Red flags flap like crazy, especially since the novel opens with Abby may go to prison for murder. (Cue dramatic music.)

As Abby begins to suspect Monica isn’t who she claims to be, things unravel at breakneck speed. Suddenly it’s not just her marriage or future baby on the line—it’s her very survival. And just when you think it can’t get worse, McFadden tosses in a few more curveballs.

While the ending didn’t land with the explosive force I hoped for, and a few plot points were admittedly far-fetched, I still tore through this book in just a few hours. It grabbed my attention and didn’t let go—and honestly, that’s what I’m here for. McFadden delivers her signature suspense-soaked ride, and I’m always ready to buckle in.

Plus, the sneak peek of her upcoming novel Intruder at the end? Chef’s kiss. That was the cherry on top—or, more accurately, the icing on the cheesecake.

Four stars from me. Another thrilling ride from the queen of twists that slap you in the face and leave you grinning like a maniac.

Many thanks to NetGalley and Poisoned Pen Press for sharing another unputdownable Freida McFadden digital reviewer copy with me in exchange for my honest thoughts. I’m already counting down to the next one.

[2.5⭐] 𝙏𝙝𝙚 𝙎𝙪𝙧𝙧𝙤𝙜𝙖𝙩𝙚 𝙈𝙤𝙩𝙝𝙚𝙧 es un thriller psicológico escrito por Freida McFadden y publicado en 2018. La novela nos presenta a Abby, una mujer que desea ser madre más que cualquier otra cosa, pero que tras años de tratamientos de fertilidad fallidos siente que la maternidad es un sueño imposible. Todo cambia cuando su asistente personal, Mónica, le ofrece convertirse en su madre subrogada.


Esto es lo que pasa cuando has leído mucho a una autora: se te hace repetitivo.
Mientras avanzaba en la lectura no podía evitar sentir que estaba ante una especie de borrador de varias ideas que la escritora ha ido puliendo con los años. Siento que esta historia es una mezcla de varias otras novelas suyas, pero en una versión más primaria. Es como si aquí estuvieran las semillas de lo que después perfeccionó en libros posteriores. Cuando ya conoces la “fórmula”, el efecto sorpresa pierde fuerza.

Esta novela es la más evidente de todas. Desde muy temprano se sabe hacia dónde va la historia: se intuye quién no es quien dice ser y se sospecha qué va a suceder. Incluso, uno anticipa los famosos “plot twists” antes de que ocurran, no fue nada emocionante leerla en ese sentido.

El tema del vientre de alquiler o la maternidad subrogada me pareció interesante. No había leído antes un thriller que abordara este conflicto desde ese ángulo y eso le da un punto a favor. Hay un potencial enorme en esa premisa: el deseo desesperado de ser madre, la vulnerabilidad emocional y la confianza puesta en otra mujer que literalmente lleva tu sueño en el cuerpo. Es un terreno ideal para la paranoia, la manipulación y el terror psicológico.
El problema es que la ejecución se quedó corta.

Además, está ese típico elemento que hace recordar a Millie en 𝙇𝙖 𝙖𝙨𝙞𝙨𝙩𝙚𝙣𝙩𝙖: ese constante “esto es rarísimo, pero lo dejaré pasar” que el personaje principal repite una y otra vez (esa decisión de ignorar señales evidentes para que la trama avance).

Abby, como narradora única, está construida para que dudemos de su percepción, algo muy característico de la autora. Sin embargo, aquí el juego no es tan fino porque no hay suficiente ambigüedad real como para que el lector caiga en la trampa. El título mismo prácticamente anuncia el conflicto central.

A pesar de todo, la novela tiene una narrativa dinámica y rápida de leer, algo muy característico en la autora. Los capítulos son cortos, los finales de los capítulos tienen pequeñas tensiones y el ritmo es ágil. De hecho, creo que si esta hubiese sido mi primera experiencia con la autora, probablemente la habría disfrutado más, pero cuando vienes de leer sus novelas más pulidas, se nota la diferencia.
No le pongo tan mala nota precisamente porque es de sus inicios y hay una clara evolución narrativa en sus obras posteriores. Se percibe que aquí todavía estaba afinando su estilo, probando estructuras y consolidando esa voz que después se volvió tan reconocible.

Si no conociera el potencial de Freida, quizás la evaluación sería distinta. Le hubiese puesto un 2 porque sé lo que puede hacer, he leído libros suyos que realmente me dejaron sorprendida. Sin embargo, no lo hago porque entiendo que esta novela forma parte de su proceso de crecimiento como escritora y también porque, pese a todo, no me aburrí.

El clímax, que debería ser explosivo, se siente más como una confirmación de lo que ya uno había ido sospechando. El clásico momento en que el “villano” explica su motivación está ahí, pero no me generó impacto, sino cierta sensación de déjà vu. No hay ese “wow moment” (como dirían los Power Peralta) que una va persiguiendo cuando toma un thriller psicológico.


Finalmente, puedo decir que 𝙏𝙝𝙚 𝙎𝙪𝙧𝙧𝙤𝙜𝙖𝙩𝙚 𝙈𝙤𝙩𝙝𝙚𝙧 es una historia con una premisa potente y narrada con el ritmo ágil que caracteriza a la autora, pero que se siente demasiado débil en su desarrollo. Es evidente, es formulaica y, para quienes ya hemos leído varios de sus libros, resulta repetitiva. Aun así, me parece interesante verla como un punto de partida dentro de su trayectoria.

When a woman is desperate for a child, anything can happen.

And "anything" is exactly what happens in Freida McFadden's "The Surrogate Mother."

Although "The Surrogate Mother" was not my favorite "surrogate thriller" and/or "Freida book", it was a compelling, fast-paced. and entertaining drama that was intriguing from beginning to end.

Yes, it was predictable and yes, it had many "this would never happen" implausible moments.

But it featured author Freida McFadden's classic misdirections, twists, and unreliable narrators -- making this quick-and-easy read a winner.

I listened to the audiobook and narrator Alyson Crawchuk did a superb job with the narration.

This is my 7th book by author Freida McFadden and I am a fan.

When the next Freida book is released, I'M IN!

This is my review of The Surrogate Mother.

Abby had a good job in advertising, a great marriage to husband, Sam, a math professor, and she came from a well-off family.

But Abby was missing one thing, to make the picture complete…Abby wanted a baby more than anything.

After years of failed infertility treatments and adoptions that had fallen through, it seemed like motherhood was not in her future. But then her personal assistant Monica made a generous offer that made all of Abby's dreams come true.

Monica offers to be Abby’s surrogate. Sam and Abby will compensate Monica by sending her to graduate school. After much consideration, Abby and her husband except Monica as a surrogate. The plan is now in place and Abby couldn’t be happier!

This novel has so many twists, that it kept me on my toes. Another great book by McFadden! I am so impressed with this author that I will continue to read all of her novels.
